deals.evidence: officially announce the formation of Austin FC, Major League Soccer's 27th team.
deals.headline: MLS formally launches Austin FC, its 27th club, under Anthony Precourt
deals.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber and Austin FC chairman/CEO Anthony Precourt announced the formation of Austin FC as MLS's 27th team. Precourt Sports Ventures had owned the Columbus Crew and planned to move it to Austin; the Crew was instead sold to a local group, and PSV had agreed a stadium deal with the City of Austin for city-owned land at McKalla Place the month before. No fee is stated.

deals.date_text: Announced 23 August 2019 (two further members confirmed September 2019)
deals.evidence: The participants in the investor syndicate include Mr. Margain, Matthew McConaughey, Marius Haas, Bryan Sheffield, David Kahn, and Toby Neugebauer.
deals.headline: Margain-led local syndicate, including Matthew McConaughey, buys into Austin FC
deals.investor: Investor syndicate led by Eddie Margain's Pixiu Investments (Margain, Matthew McConaughey, Marius Haas, Bryan Sheffield, David Kahn, Toby Neugebauer)
deals.summary: Jackson Walker, counsel to the investors, states that an investor syndicate led by Eddie Margain and his firm Pixiu Investments took an ownership interest in Austin FC, announced on 23 August 2019; Margain became alternate governor and McConaughey 'Minister of Culture'. Amounts and stakes were not disclosed.

deals.evidence: Two Oak privately funded the $260 million venue, which opened in 2021, but it is owned by the city.
deals.headline: Austin FC's parent privately funds the $260m Q2 Stadium, owned by the city
deals.summary: Sportico reports that Two Oak Ventures, the company that owns Austin FC, privately funded the $260 million Q2 Stadium, which opened in 2021 and is owned by the City of Austin. The financing structure is not described.

deals.evidence: in a series of transactions that assigned the MLS club an enterprise value of more than $900 million
deals.headline: Five local investors buy into Austin FC at an enterprise value above $900m
deals.investor: Jenny Just and Matt Hulsizer (PEAK6 co-founders), Tench Coxe, Dave Snyderman, Tanuj Gulati
deals.summary: Sportico reports that five new minority owners joined Two Oak Ventures in a series of transactions valuing the club at an enterprise value of more than $900 million (later reported as about $912 million); who sold and how much was bought were not disclosed, all prior backers remain, Precourt stays majority owner and Hulsizer becomes alternate governor. Inner Circle Sports ran the process.

deals.evidence: are part of the group that recently invested in Austin FC at an enterprise value of $912 million
deals.headline: Borgen family's FirstTracks joins Austin FC at a $912m enterprise value, completing the equity raise
deals.summary: Austin FC announced that FirstTracks Sports Ventures, managed by Jon-Erik Borgen and affiliated with the Borgen Investment Group (a Denver single-family asset management firm), acquired a non-controlling minority stake, completing the planned equity raise. Sportico puts the enterprise value of the 2025 transactions at about $912 million.

deals.evidence: have acquired non-controlling minority stakes in the Club from Pixiu Sports
deals.headline: David Booth and Garheng Kong buy minority stakes in Austin FC from Pixiu Sports
deals.summary: Austin FC announced that Dimensional Fund Advisors founder David Booth and HealthQuest Capital founder Garheng Kong acquired non-controlling minority stakes from Pixiu Sports, which stays in the ownership group; Precourt keeps majority ownership and operating control. Terms were not disclosed.

name: Austin FC
notes: US clubs publish no accounts: revenue ($94m) and operating income ($5m, EBITDA) are Forbes estimates for the 2025 MLS season from the Feb 2026 MLS list (cited via its Wayback Machine copy; forbes.com/sites blocks scripts); the Forbes May 2026 team page repeats the $855M value. Sportico's own 2025 MLS valuation put Austin FC at $865m with 2024 revenue estimated at $96m (same Sportico articles). The 2025 transactions were at an enterprise value of about $912m (Sportico, Oct 2025); no stake sizes or prices are disclosed for any owner. 'Pixiu Sports', the seller to Booth and Kong in 2026, is not described on the club's page; the 2019 syndicate was led by Margain's Pixiu Investments (Jackson Walker). Owner since_year comes from the announcement pages cited per owner; Agatha Precourt's entry date is not stated. Capacity is the 2021 figure (20,738 = 100% capacity, KEYE); Forbes lists 20,700. Attendance is the 2021 average (every match sold out); Sportico reported 87 straight sellouts by Oct 2025, but no 2025 average was found. Andy Loughnane became CEO in Aug 2026 (Precourt had been CEO since 2019). No league titles. Registry number for Austin TeamCo LLC and social follower counts not found.

ownership_summary: Austin FC is owned through Two Oak Ventures, which also runs its academy, MLS Next Pro team and Q2 Stadium. Founder and chairman Anthony Precourt, with his family, keeps majority ownership and operating control (through Precourt Sports Ventures). The minority owners are the 2019 syndicate led by co-founder Eddie Margain's Pixiu Investments (Matthew McConaughey, Marius Haas, Bryan Sheffield, David Kahn, Toby Neugebauer); five 2025 investors (Jenny Just and Matt Hulsizer, Tench Coxe, Dave Snyderman, Tanuj Gulati); the Borgen family's FirstTracks Sports Ventures, whose October 2025 entry completed the equity raise at an enterprise value Sportico put at about $912m; and David Booth and Garheng Kong, who bought stakes from Pixiu Sports in September 2026. No stake percentages are disclosed.
